chunks: Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Ibn Abi Umayr from some of his companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: "Do you know why the standing (at Mina) was made for three days?" I said: "For what reason was it made, or for what purpose?" He said: "Whoever attains any one of them has attained the Hajj."
ai.seo_question: Why is the standing at Mina for three days considered sufficient for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the three-day stay in Mina is a comprehensive fulfillment of Hajj rites rather than a rigid minimum, as even a partial stay validates the pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations, distinguishing between the essential pillar of standing at Arafat and the supplementary acts in Mina. It reflects the broader theological emphasis on the spirit of worship over mere formalistic duration.
